sourceClaims.label: The report reviews shared/notify.ts and its mirrored tests/shared/notify.test.ts owner.
Every case builds fresh state inline without shared mutable fixtures or setup hooks.
The owner uses ordered phase comments and descriptive production-role naming.
Data-driven rows create one sibling test per row.
Most cases compare complete hand-authored rendered values and prove severity, token, and reason orthogonality.
Severity, reload-hint, and tally helpers generally reduce caller-stamped fields instead of re-deriving them from status.
About nineteen owner cases use substring, prefix, or suffix assertions as their only content check although complete output is known.
Those fragment-only cases can pass with wrong tokens, order, or row membership.
Replace genuinely weak fragment-only checks with independently hand-authored complete notification values.
The already-no-autoupdate marketplace case asserts only call and argument counts and never inspects the rendered body.
Add a complete expected notification argument for the zero-content case.
Several fragment assertions are redundant because the same cases already compare the complete output.
Remove redundant fragment checks or preserve their intent in the case title.
The owner casts hand-built context, API, and some message values through as never at every notification entrypoint.
Those casts erase compiler checking of the doubles and message values.
The historical report attributed every cast to notify's use of the full ExtensionContext and ExtensionAPI interfaces.
Notification message construction drifts between explicit annotations and satisfies checks and should be standardized on satisfies.
One synchronous edge case patches String.prototype.lastIndexOf and manually restores the test mock tracker.
The prototype patch is shared-process mutation, the manual restore is redundant, and a safer seam or explicit rationale is preferable.
Notification entrypoints accept wide host interfaces although this module consumes only ui.notify and getAllTools.
Narrow consumer-declared context and soft-dependency ports could simplify the owner test without changing production callers.
notify performs a deliberate bounded render-time soft-dependency probe that does not affect status, severity, or reload state.
The historical report proposed moving the soft-dependency probe into row-producing orchestrators so notify can drop its API parameter.
The plugin-info severity arm is a deliberate closed status lookup and does not currently produce an incorrect result.
notify.ts remains a 4217-line module combining type vocabulary, grammar, severity and tally, info rendering, and dispatch concerns.
The module can be split behind the documented notify.ts import surface along layered acyclic concern boundaries.
redactAbsolutePaths and comparison helpers are reusable leaf utilities that may belong outside the presentation module.
The historical review reported no executed owner test, direct coverage, lint, or typecheck command.
The historical branch and line coverage assessment was manual and required an independent direct-coverage run.
notify-context and notify-reasons were excluded from this report's owner scope.
The historical review did not independently scan the rest of the extension for direct ui.notify calls.
The report reviews the three transaction production modules and their three mirrored owner tests.
The transaction area was historically the strongest reviewed area.
phase-ledger cases compare one shared cross-phase event log and cover forward, reverse, own-undo, containment, and undo-failure behavior.
rollback cases use independently authored whole structured values and identity checks where structural Error comparison is insufficient.
with-state-guard cases use case-owned temporary roots and controlled promises rather than sleeps or another process.
The fixing pass should add null and non-ELOCKED-code acquisition cases to close the claimed isLockHeldError branch gap.
The fixing pass should inject a narrow lock port so tests do not patch proper-lockfile's module singleton.
The fixing pass should group with-state-guard cases under describes for the two exported entrypoints.
SCHEDULE_TYPE_EVIDENCE is an undocumented compile-time-only phase fixture that is immediately void-discarded.
The phase fixture should gain a purpose comment.
The rest of phase-ledger.test.ts satisfies order, error, identity, and rollback-partial requirements.
rollback.test.ts had no findings and already proves complete structured outcomes and identities.
formatRollbackError returns structured data rather than rendered text, so whole structured-value assertions are the applicable rule.
The historical review claimed isLockHeldError lacked null and wrong-code false-arm coverage.
Add acquisition failures for null and an Error carrying a non-ELOCKED code.
The owner file uses flat top-level cases rather than describe groups per exported entrypoint.
The historical report prescribed describe groups as a project guideline requirement.
Several cases use hand-written shared persistence logs or counters around injected load and save functions.
The historical report prescribed replacing shared call logs with independent t.mock.fn call lists.
Seven acquisition and release cases patch the imported proper-lockfile singleton with t.mock.method.
An injected lock port would remove the third-party singleton patching while preserving hermeticity.
phase-ledger.ts is a pure function with documented exports and no hidden dependencies.
rollback.ts is pure, documented, and free of unsafe assertions.
with-state-guard.ts imports and calls proper-lockfile directly without a consumer-owned injection port.
Add a narrow lock provider beside the existing load and save dependency seam.
LockedStateTransaction and LockedStateTransactionDeps are exported without adjacent JSDoc.
Add short role documentation to both exported transaction interfaces.
The historical review ran no owner test, direct coverage, lint, or full check command.
The historical isLockHeldError coverage claim was derived statically and explicitly required direct-coverage confirmation.
